summary.text: Thomas Kucer is the Democratic candidate for the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, District 176, in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Jack Rader (R).
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a union sheet metal worker of more than 40 years and a resident of Hamilton Township, Pennsylvania.

paragraphs.text: Thomas Kucer earned a bachelor's degree from the National Labor College in 2013, and his career experience includes working as a construction worker.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he holds a bachelor's degree in construction management with a minor in labor relations, and that he has worked as a union sheet metal worker for more than 40 years, commuting from Pennsylvania to New York City for work.
The survey states that he has lived in Hamilton Township for 23 years.
Kucer won the Democratic primary for District 176 on May 19, 2026, as a write-in candidate.

In the survey, his campaign priorities include housing affordability and higher wages, restoring health care subsidies that were eliminated in 2026, attracting business investment and supporting Department of Labor-accredited apprenticeship programs on publicly funded projects, and protecting farmland and the environment while supporting responsible growth.
